items.stem: A team repeatedly misses its iteration goals because work is pulled in mid-iteration by a manager outside the team. What is the Scrum Master's most appropriate first action?

options.text: Coach the stakeholder and team on protecting iteration scope and using the backlog for new requests
options.rationale: Correct: a servant-leader Scrum Master addresses the systemic impediment by coaching stakeholders and reinforcing WIP/scope agreements.

options.text: Tell the team to work overtime to absorb the extra work
options.rationale: This hides the impediment and harms sustainable pace; it does not address the cause.

options.text: Add the new work silently to the current iteration
options.rationale: Accepting unmanaged scope change undermines predictability and the team's commitment.

options.text: Escalate immediately to the RTE before speaking with anyone
options.rationale: Escalation may follow, but the Scrum Master should first coach locally; jumping straight to escalation skips the servant-leader role.

items.explanation: Correct: a servant-leader Scrum Master addresses the systemic impediment by coaching stakeholders and reinforcing WIP/scope agreements.

items.stem: During PI Planning, two teams discover a dependency that cannot be resolved within the planned iterations. Where is this best captured and made visible?

options.text: On the program board as a dependency with a planned resolution
options.rationale: Correct: the program (ART planning) board visualizes cross-team dependencies and milestones so they can be managed.

options.text: In a private note kept by one Scrum Master
options.rationale: A private note is not transparent and will not be managed across the ART.

options.text: Only in the team's iteration backlog
options.rationale: The iteration backlog does not make the cross-team nature of the dependency visible.

options.text: Deferred to the next PI with no record
options.rationale: Deferring without a record loses the dependency and risks the PI objectives.

items.explanation: Correct: the program (ART planning) board visualizes cross-team dependencies and milestones so they can be managed.

items.stem: Which TWO behaviours are consistent with a Scrum Master acting as a servant leader on the ART? (Select TWO)

options.text: Removing impediments the team cannot resolve on its own
options.rationale: Correct: unblocking the team is a core servant-leader responsibility.

options.text: Facilitating team events so the team can self-organize
options.rationale: Correct: facilitation that builds the team's own capability is servant leadership.

options.text: Assigning tasks to each team member each morning
Approving all design decisions before work begins
options.rationale: Centralizing decisions removes team ownership and is not servant leadership.

options.text: Reporting individual productivity metrics to management
options.rationale: Individual surveillance metrics damage trust and are not a servant-leader practice.

items.explanation: Correct: unblocking the team is a core servant-leader responsibility.
